dedupe_keys.name: can mirgu can bus attack dataset from moving vehicles

description: CAN-MIRGU is a CAN bus attack dataset collected from a modern car with autonomous driving capabilities while it was driven in real-world scenarios. It holds benign traffic logs from six driving days and attack logs grouped as masquerade attacks, suspension attacks and physically verified real attacks such as a brake-warning attack, with a JSON file describing each attack. Its purpose is to give intrusion detection research a realistic, validated benchmark from a moving vehicle. The authors are researchers at Robert Gordon University, and the dataset was presented at the Symposium on Vehicles Security and Privacy (VehicleSec) 2024 of the Internet Society. Coverage: one vehicle, recorded on real roads; the make and model are not named in the README. Access: the README links the files in a public Google Drive folder, with a paper and video. Licence and cost: free to download; there is no licence file, so reuse terms are limited to the citation request. Caveats: a single vehicle limits generality, and the Google Drive hosting may not be permanent. It supports cyber-physical resilience and attack propagation studies for road vehicles and is the real-vehicle counterpart of the synthetic SynCAN dataset catalogued in the same pass.
